Profit Margin vs. ROI for Resellers

Understand what each percentage measures and when each one helps.

Profit margin and ROI answer different questions. Margin measures profit relative to revenue. ROI measures profit relative to the money invested.

Profit margin = net profit ÷ selling price × 100
ROI = net profit ÷ total investment × 100

One sale, two useful percentages

If an item sells for $75, produces $25 in net profit, and required $30 of total investment, its margin is 33.33% while its ROI is 83.33%.

Margin helps you understand how much room a sale has for discounts, returns, and unexpected costs. ROI helps compare sourcing opportunities that require different amounts of cash.

Use both, not either

A high ROI on a very cheap item may still produce too few dollars for the time involved. A healthy dollar profit with a weak ROI may tie up too much capital. Compare net profit, margin, ROI, time, and expected sell-through together. Check a scenario with the ROI calculator.

Keep the estimate honest.

Fee structures and actual costs can change. Verify the rules that apply to your sale and treat every result as planning information.
